dct_description_sm: An ecologically and socially important terrestrial species that may be impacted by climate is the caribou. Recent studies have indicated that the George River caribou herd has suffered a dramatic population decline. Modifications in the distribution of the caribou and its habitat due to altered temperature and precipitation regimes and effects such as food availability, predator's density and human disturbance that also correlate with climate change have social and economic implications for the Naskapi Nation who are dependent on the caribou for their livelihood. The purpose of this project was to: (1) deepen the understanding of the impacts of climate change on the caribou, the land and Naskapi society; (2) identify the impacts for which it is necessary to be especially careful; (3) develop tools, community monitoring processes, and guidance documents that will help to adapt to the impacts of climate change on the caribou, the land, and resource use in the Naskapi territory in ways that are appropriate to the Naskapi context; (4) increase awareness about climate change and foster Naskapi participation in participating in finding climate change strategies; and (5) train young Naskapi in climate change and caribou monitoring.
